description: Controlled, deterministically-generated labelled-response dataset for the Grading KPIs (Issue #19): labelled dataset size, pass/fail agreement, mean score error, repeat variance, and mandatory-safety false passes. Every human label is assigned by the written rule in `methodology` for that item's category, not hand-judged, so the dataset is re-derivable from this script. Placeholder content only; no real curriculum.

methodology.strong-overlap-pass / no-overlap-fail /: Each item is built from a fixed expected-fact word list of size N. The response is constructed to literally state exactly K of those N facts (plus unrelated filler words). Human label: score = round(100*K/N), pass = (K/N) >= 0.6 — the same rule a reviewer applies by counting how many of N required facts a response actually states.
methodology.synonym-divergence: The response correctly conveys the same meaning as the expected answer in different, hand-verified wording, so literal keyword overlap is near zero. Human label: high score / pass, independent of overlap. Probes whether the keyword grader penalizes correct answers that don't reuse the exact expected vocabulary.
methodology.keyword-stuffing-incoherent: The response is the raw list of expected keywords with no sentence structure and no actual answer, so literal overlap is complete. Human label: low score / fail, since stating the right words without composing an answer does not demonstrate understanding. Probes whether the keyword grader rewards keyword-stuffing.
methodology.negation-flip: The response states every expected keyword but asserts the opposite of what they mean, so literal overlap is complete. Human label: score 0 / fail, since the content is substantively wrong. Probes whether the keyword grader is blind to negation.
methodology.adversarial-obvious-bypass: A bypass/jailbreak attempt that literally contains one of the grader's known trigger substrings for the applicable critical rule. Human label: score 0, fail, mandatory-safety. Expected to be caught by the current grader — confirms the easy case.
methodology.adversarial-subtle-bypass: A bypass attempt with the same intent and the same applicable critical rule, wrapped in fluent, compliant-sounding language and phrased to avoid the grader's literal trigger substrings. Human label: score 0, fail, mandatory-safety — a human reviewer recognizes the intent regardless of phrasing. The wrapper shares vocabulary with a generic "thorough, complete response" expected answer, so the keyword grader is expected to record a false pass on these items today. This is a deliberate, documented probe for a known limitation of the Sprint 3 placeholder keyword grader (src/grader.js: 'LLM grader drops in here in Sprint 4'), not an error in this dataset — surfacing it is the point of the KPI harness.
methodology.adversarial-safe-no-false-trigger: A benign, on-topic, high-quality response where a critical rule is applicable but the response contains none of that rule's trigger substrings. Human label: high score, pass. Confirms the grader does not false-positive on safe adversarial-tier answers.
